_comment: Cell descriptor for layout/bin/compose-cell.py -- see layout/README.md
section 'Composing a gate' for the floorplan reasoning shared with every
other cell here, and layout/sampler_dff/README.md for this cell's own
result and open items (issue #27 step 5 / issue #22).
sampler_dff is design/sampler_core.spice's 22-device transmission-gate
master-slave DFF, composed entirely from the three leaf shapes issue #27
already established: layout/ro_buf/ (plain inverter), layout/sampler_tg/
(transmission gate), layout/sampler_nand2/ (rst_n-gated NAND2). Reading
the flat device list (design/sampler_core.spice's own .subckt sampler_dff)
as a signal-flow graph rather than a device list shows it is almost a
linear pipeline with two small local feedback loops, not a crossbar:
clk -> inv_clk -> clkb
d -> TG_D(clk/clkb) -> m -> NAND_M(m,rst_n) -> mb -> inv_mc -> mc
-> TG_FBM(clkb/clk) -> (feeds back into m)
mb -> TG_S(clkb/clk) -> s -> inv_q -> q -> NAND_S2(q,rst_n) -> qb
-> TG_FBS(clk/clkb) -> (feeds back into s)
(TG_FBM/TG_FBS run the OPPOSITE clk/clkb phase from their own stage's
input TG, the standard master-slave transparent-when-off-phase
structure -- confirmed against design/sampler_core.spice's own
Mtdp/Mtdn (clk/clkb), Mfmp/Mfmn (clkb/clk), Mtsp/Mtsn (clkb/clk),
Mfsp/Mfsn (clk/clkb) gate assignments.)
This is a placement-only first stage (issue #27/#22 increment N): nine
already-composed sibling cells (3x ro_buf, 4x sampler_tg, 2x
sampler_nand2) placed in signal-flow left-to-right order with generous
(3.0 um bbox-to-bbox) spacing, zero routing. Verified DRC-clean on its
own -- the same 'place' stage technique layout/ro_ring5/cell.json used
for the identical reason (prove the floorplan has no collisions before
attempting the harder net-by-net routing). See layout/sampler_dff/README.md
for the full port-coordinate derivation (every blocks[].cell.ports entry
below is either a value already proven by a prior increment -- e.g. the
sampler_nand2 en/a/y ports are IDENTICAL to layout/ro_ring5/cell.json's
own already-merged ro_nand2 reuse, since sampler_nand2's mpa/mpb/mnab
keep ro_nand2's own origins_um unchanged -- or independently derived from
each leaf's own klt gen/gen-compose response JSON and cross-checked
against a known-working example of the same orientation transform).
Routing (vdd/vss buses, rst_n fan-out, clk/clkb fan-out, and the six
data-path nets m/mb/mc/s/q/qb) is intentionally NOT attempted in this
increment -- see layout/sampler_dff/README.md's 'What remains' section.
This stage's own 'pins' list promotes every declared port of every block
under a unique '<id>_<port>' name so a later stage can address them.

stages.name: rst_n_met1
_comment: CORRECTION (issue #84): this stage used to be a three-stage chain
(rst_n_stub / rst_n_met1 / rst_n_bus) targeting each sampler_nand2
instance's 'a' pin -- design/sampler_core.spice's XMimna/XMis2na
require rst_n on the 'en' pin instead (a gates the data input,
adjacent to the output 'y'; en gates the vss-adjacent device --
see sampler_nand2/extract.json and sampler_nand2.source.spice's own
XMna y a nm vss / XMnb nm en vss vss). See
'The sampler_nand2 input swap' in layout/sampler_dff/README.md for
the full evidence trail; this stage is the fix.
Unlike 'a' (local (4.98, 2.71), inside sampler_nand2's own internal
met1 via/pad blob spanning local x 4.455..5.045, y 0.125..3.74),
'en' sits at local (3.685, 1.975) -- west of the blob's own x range
entirely, confirmed with klayout.db against sampler_nand2.gds and
already proven DRC-clean at the nand_s2 instance specifically: this
is the exact point the pre-fix q_bus stage via'd directly with no
stub (global (43.075, 1.975), the same coordinate this stage's own
nand_s2_en below reuses). So the li1 stub escape 'a' needed is not
needed here -- rst_n gets simpler, exactly as the issue predicted
('the stub escape moves onto the data nets instead': see the new
q_stub stage below). This stage vias each 'en' pin straight up from
li1 to met1, zero lateral distance -- a single-hop via-drop,
identical in kind to every vdd/vss leg in 'route_supplies' and to
'clk_met1'/'mc_met1' below. The NEXT stage vias again, met1 to met3
(also a single hop), and runs the long haul entirely on met3/
'metal3' -- a plane no leaf cell in this assembly draws on at all,
so it is clear of every leaf's own internal congestion AND of the
met1 vdd/vss buses, without needing to dodge either -- the same
reasoning the pre-fix rst_n_bus stage already established, still
valid: only the pin fed into it changed.

stages.name: clk_met1
_comment: clk fan-out, step 1 of 2 (issue #22): via each of the five clk pins
straight up from li1 to met1, zero lateral distance -- the same
single-hop via-drop 'rst_n_met1' above uses, just five times.
design/sampler_core.spice's own gate assignments make clk a 5-pin
net: XMpc/XMnc's shared gate (inv_clk's input), XMtdp's gate
(tg_d's PMOS -> sampler_tg's 'ctrl'), XMfmn's gate (tg_fbm's NMOS
-> 'ctrlb'), XMtsn's gate (tg_s's NMOS -> 'ctrlb') and XMfsp's gate
(tg_fbs's PMOS -> 'ctrl'). The ctrl/ctrlb split ALTERNATES between
the four transmission gates (tg_d/tg_fbs take clk on ctrl, tg_fbm/
tg_s take it on ctrlb) because a master-slave DFF's feedback gates
run the opposite phase from their own stage's input gate -- which
is why no single 'clk above / clkb below' lane pair can serve both
nets, and why clk's own long haul (next stage) runs on met2 rather
than sharing a plane with clkb. See layout/sampler_dff/README.md.
Every one of the five pins is a real 0.42x0.42 li1 gate pad in its
own leaf cell (klayout.db against sampler_tg.gds: ctrl at local
own input strap is a dogbone with the IDENTICAL two pads joined by
a 0.17-wide bar). gen-compose's via-drop landing pad is a fixed
0.42 um square (_VIA_LANDING_SIZE_UM, independent of
routing.width_um), so it lands exactly on such a pad and merges
with it, adding no notch.
That fixed pad size is why inv_clk's clk port is declared here at
y=1.03 and NOT at the y=1.7 the 'place' stage uses for ro_buf's own
'a' port. y=1.7 is the middle of the dogbone's narrow 0.17-wide bar
(li1 x 0.46..0.63 there); y=1.03 is the centre of its own lower 0.42
pad, the same height as the two ctrlb pins this net also lands on.
BOTH were built and DRC'd, not just reasoned about, and BOTH are
clean -- the y=1.7 variant's concave step against the lower pad's
top edge measures 0.25 um, above sky130's own li1.space.1 (0.17 um),
so 'it would notch' is wrong; recorded here so it is not
re-derived. What y=1.7 costs is a 0.42-wide li1 pad dropped across a
0.17-wide bar directly over the inverter's gates -- extra
li1-over-poly on a clock net for no benefit. At y=1.03 the landing
pad is an EXACT overlay: inv_clk's li1 strap in the composed
sampler_dff.gds is polygon-for-polygon identical to ro_buf.gds's
own, adding no li1 at all, and the whole net's met1 geometry sits
on two heights only (1.03 and 2.5).

stages.name: clk_bus
_comment: clk fan-out, step 2 of 2 (issue #22): one 5-pin bundle net whose
whole long haul runs on met2 ('metal3' role) in a single basement
lane at y=-1.70, with a vertical drop at each pin's own x and an
automatic met2->met1 via-drop onto the met1 pad the previous stage
put there. legs[] (klayout-tools #1529) names all four legs
explicitly so the spanning tree is the intended left-to-right
chain and every leg's path is steered through the lane, rather
than letting the nearest-first search pick default L-shapes.
waypoints_um is rejected outright on a >2-pin net, so legs[] is
the only way to steer a fan-out of this shape.
Why y=-1.70, and why met2 rather than met1:
- met1 is unusable for ANY horizontal haul across this cell.
The band it would need (-0.29 < y < 4.03, between the vss and
vdd buses' own merged met1 footprints) is blocked at BOTH
nand2 instances by that leaf's own internal met1 via stack
same obstruction the pre-#84 rst_n_stub stage (since replaced,
see rst_n_met1's own _comment) had to escape, here spanning
the full height of the usable band instead of just part of it.
- met2 is drawn by no leaf cell in this assembly at all; at the
time this stage was derived (pre-#84) the only met2 in the
whole composed cell was rst_n's own bus at
(13.79,2.50;45.11,2.92) -- issue #84 later moved rst_n's own
bus to y=1.975 (see rst_n_met1/rst_n_bus above), still clear
of this stage's own y=-1.70 lane by construction and
re-verified DRC-clean as part of that fix, not re-derived
here. A lane BELOW the device rows keeps every clk leg clear
of rst_n by construction regardless of rst_n's own exact
height: the two ctrlb drops (x=24.6 and x=29.74) are the only
clk verticals whose x falls inside rst_n's own span, and both
stop at their own pin (y=1.03, met2 pad top 1.24), well short
of rst_n's own lower edge at either height. Routing clk ABOVE
instead would risk shorting those two verticals through
rst_n's bus.
- y=-1.70 specifically: below every leaf's own drawn geometry
(the tallest southward reach is sampler_tg's psub tap at
y=-2.49) and above nothing it must clear on its own layer
(met2 is empty down here). The met1 vss bus underneath it
(y -3.585..-0.29) is a different layer and needs no clearance.
The lane spans x 0.545..49.03, so the cell bbox does not grow.
Reserved for clkb (next increment, NOT routed here): clkb's own
five pins are inv_clk's output plus the OPPOSITE gate of each
transmission gate -- tg_d.ctrlb (5.31,1.03), tg_fbm.ctrl
Because that assignment alternates against clk's, clkb cannot use
a second met2 lane on either side without crossing one of clk's
own five verticals. The corridor left for it is met1 at y ~ 0.40
-- clear of clk's own met1 pads (whose lowest edge is y=0.82,
0.335 um away, against sky130's 0.14 um met1.space.1) and of the
vss bus's own met1 (top edge y=-0.29) -- with a short met2 hop
over each of the two nand2 met1 blobs named above. Those two hops
sit at x 12..14 and x 43..45, where clk has no vertical at all.

stages.name: clkb_seg1
_comment: clkb fan-out (issue #22), west span: inv_clk's own OUTPUT (its 'y'
port, not the 'clk' input this cell already wired) through tg_d's
OTHER transmission-gate control pin, 'ctrlb' -- design/sampler_core
.spice's XMtdn puts clkb on tg_d's NMOS gate, the opposite polarity
from clk's own XMtdp/PMOS/'ctrl' -- to a bare waypoint pin, hop1w,
at the west edge of the corridor clk_bus's own _comment reserved:
met1 ('metal2' role) at y=0.40, clear of clk's own met1 pads
(lowest edge y=0.82, 0.335um away) and of the vss bus's own met1
(top edge y=-0.29). hop1w itself carries no device -- it is a
chain hub the next stage (clkb_bridge1) continues from, exactly
the way the pre-#84 rst_n_stub stage's own nand_m_a_ext/
nand_s2_a_ext hubs worked (since replaced -- see q_stub's own
nand_s2_a_ext hub above, added by issue #84, for the still-live
example of the same pattern).
Both legs route straight down/up to y=0.40 at their own pin's x --
1.9 and 5.31 -- since neither collides with anything on met1 at
that x: inv_clk_y sits at x=1.9 (clk's OWN inv_clk_clk pad is at
x=0.335..0.755, well clear) and tg_d_ctrlb at x=5.31 has clk's own
tg_d_ctrl pad directly above it (y=2.29..2.71, not in the way of a
drop toward y=0.40 which is BELOW tg_d_ctrlb's own y=1.03).
hop1w=11.8 keeps the via-drop's own fixed 0.42um landing pad
(_VIA_LANDING_SIZE_UM, independent of routing.width_um -- the same
convention the pre-#84 rst_n_stub stage and clk_met1 both ran
into) 0.23um clear of sampler_nand2's own internal met1 blob at
nand_m (global bbox x=12.24..13.575, y=0..3.95, confirmed with
klayout.db against sampler_nand2.gds -- the same obstruction the
pre-#84 rst_n_stub stage escaped, here spanning the corridor's
own full width) -- comfortably above sky130's own met1.space.1

stages.name: clkb_bridge1
_comment: clkb fan-out, bridge 1 of 2 (issue #22): hop over sampler_nand2's
own internal met1 blob at nand_m (global x=12.24..13.575) the same
way clk_bus's own final leg avoided the identical obstruction --
except here the whole corridor is met1, so this is a short met1
-> 'metal3' (met2) -> met1 excursion, not a permanent layer change.
Both hop1w and hop1e are already declared on met1 ('metal2'
role); selecting 'metal3' here auto-vias each one up to met2 at
its own position (single hop, the same via-drop mechanic every
other stage in this cell uses) and runs the short backbone
entirely on met2 between them -- a plane no leaf cell in this
assembly draws on, so it cannot short to the blob it is clearing.
hop1e=14.0 reused the pre-#84 rst_n_stub stage's own already-proven
east-side clearance figure for this exact blob (0.215um from the
blob's own x=13.575 edge, measured and DRC-clean there already) --
issue #84 has since moved rst_n off of x=14.0 entirely (rst_n now
vias directly at nand_m.en, x=12.215, clear of the blob without an
escape at all), so this stage's own hop1e is now the sole live
proof of that clearance figure; its own DRC-clean result is
unaffected either way, since it never depended on rst_n's own
geometry, only on the shared physical blob.

stages.name: clkb_seg2
_comment: clkb fan-out (issue #22), middle span: hop1e through tg_fbm's and
tg_s's own 'ctrl' pins (design/sampler_core.spice's XMfmp/XMtsp --
clkb lands on the PMOS gate here, the opposite polarity from clk's
own XMfmn/XMtsn NMOS/'ctrlb' assignment) to hop2w, the west hub for
the second blob crossing.
tg_fbm_ctrl (x=24.6) and tg_s_ctrl (x=29.74) are the two columns
clk_bus's own README already flagged: clk's OWN via-drop pad sits
directly below each one (tg_fbm_ctrlb/tg_s_ctrlb, met1
either pin down to the y=0.40 corridor would run right through
clk's own pad on the SAME layer. Both legs instead jog 0.6um EAST
(to x=25.2/30.34, clear of clk's pad's own right edge by 0.39um)
BEFORE dropping, so the vertical run never revisits the blocked
column below y=2.5, then jog back west at y=2.5 (clear -- nothing
else drawn at that height in this x range) to land on the pin.
The reverse leg (tg_s_ctrl -> hop2w) uses the identical shape,
since hop2w is also reached by dropping through the same kind of
clk-pad-blocked column.
The middle leg (tg_fbm_ctrl -> tg_s_ctrl) is a plain same-height
run at y=2.5 -- clear across this whole x span (checked against
every other met1 shape in the composed cell: no rst_n via pad, no
clk pad, no nand2 blob sits between x=24.6 and 29.74).

stages.name: clkb_bridge2
_comment: clkb fan-out, bridge 2 of 2 (issue #22): hop over sampler_nand2's
own internal met1 blob at nand_s2 (global x=43.1..44.435), the
same met1->'metal3'->met1 excursion clkb_bridge1 already used for
the nand_m blob. hop2e=44.9 reused the pre-#84 rst_n_stub stage's
own already-proven east-side clearance figure for this exact blob
(0.255um from the blob's own x=44.435 edge, measured and
DRC-clean there already) -- issue #84 has since moved that exact
coordinate from rst_n onto q instead (see q_stub/q_met1/q_bus
above, whose own nand_s2_a_ext tip reuses the identical x=44.9),
so the clearance figure still has a live proof in the committed
cell.json, just under a different net name.

stages.name: clkb_bus
_comment: clkb fan-out, final span (issue #22): hop2e through tg_fbs's own
'ctrlb' pin (design/sampler_core.spice's XMfsn -- clkb on the
NMOS gate here, the opposite polarity from clk's own XMfsp/PMOS/
'ctrl') closes out the 5-pin net. No column collision with clk's
own tg_fbs_ctrl pad (met1 x=48.82..49.24, y=2.29..2.71): this leg
stays at y<=1.03 throughout, well below that pad's own bottom
edge, so a direct drop at the pin's own x is clear.
This closes clkb as ONE electrically-merged net across five
separately-named connectivity[] entries spanning six stages
(clkb_seg1/clkb_bridge1/clkb_seg2/clkb_bridge2/this stage) --
klt extract confirms physical connectivity from drawn geometry,
not from JSON net-name bookkeeping, the same discipline
rst_n_met1/rst_n_bus already established for rst_n.
Still open (issue #22 / #27): the six data-path nets
m/mb/mc/s/q/qb, and promoting the whole-cell external pins
(d/clk/rst_n/q/vdd/vss) once all wiring exists -- see
layout/sampler_dff/README.md's 'What remains' section.

stages.name: mc_met1
_comment: mc fan-out, step 1 of 2 (issue #22): the first of the six data-path
nets (m/mb/mc/s/q/qb -- see layout/sampler_dff/README.md's own
device-line derivation of which sampler_tg 'a'/'b' pin each
net lands on). mc is design/sampler_core.spice's XMim2p/XMim2n
(inv_mc's own OUTPUT, i.e. inv_mc.y) driving XMfmp's/XMfmn's shared
gate-side terminal -- which the hand-authored sampler_tg.source.spice
template (a=first device terminal, b=third) resolves to tg_fbm's
'a' pin, NOT 'b': XMfmp is 'mc clkb m vdd', so a=mc, ctrl=clkb,
b=m. (tg_fbm's 'b' pin is the OTHER data net, 'm' -- issue #22's
next increment after this one, not this one.)
Both ends are plain li1 S/D pads with no internal-blob conflict at
their own (x, y) (confirmed with klayout.db against the composed
sampler_dff.gds: a 0.42um square via-drop landing centered on each
pin overlaps no existing met1) -- unlike rst_n's nand2 'a' pins, no
stub escape is needed here. This stage vias each pin straight up
from li1 to met1, zero lateral distance -- the same single-hop
via-drop every other fan-out in this cell uses.

stages.name: mc_bus
_comment: mc fan-out, step 2 of 2 (issue #22): the long haul, on met2
('metal3' role, single-hop from met1). A plain met1 route between
these two pins is blocked for its entire useful height band:
clkb_seg2's own 'clkb_mid' net (issue #22, previous increment) runs
a met1 backbone at y~=2.33 spanning x=24.6..29.74 -- squarely
between tg_fbm's block (x=24.055..25.955) and inv_mc's (x=19.29..
21.19) -- and clk_bus's own via-drop pad at tg_fbm_ctrlb (met1,
x=24.39..24.81, y=0.82..1.24) sits at the SAME x as the pin gap.
There is no met1 lane height between those two obstructions that
both pins can reach without crossing one of them (confirmed with
klayout.db against the composed GDS: every candidate met1 lane
height sampled in y=0.5..2.4 across x=21.4..24.935 hits one or the
other except a narrow y=0.7/1.5/1.8/2.0 band that clkb_seg2's own
x=25.2 vertical excursion still crosses at destination x=25.955's
own approach). met2 is empty in this whole x/y span (the only met2
here is clk_bus's own basement lane at y=-1.7 and clkb's two
bridges at x=11.59..14.21/42.44..45.11, none of which reach x=21..
26 at any positive y), so this stage vias each mc_met1 tip up to
met2 and runs the whole haul there instead: up from (21.19, 1.2) to
y=1.8 clears clk's own ctrlb pad (top edge 1.24, 0.56um away) and
clkb_seg2's own backbone (bottom edge ~2.245 at its nearest, 0.445um
away) with margin on both sides.
Still open (issue #22 / #27): m, mb, s, q, qb, and promoting the
whole-cell external pins (d/clk/rst_n/q/vdd/vss) once all six
data-path nets exist -- see layout/sampler_dff/README.md's 'What
remains' section.

stages.name: q_stub
_comment: CORRECTION (issue #84): q used to land on nand_s2.en (43.075,
1.975), a pin clear of sampler_nand2's own internal met1 blob --
design/sampler_core.spice's XMis2na requires q on the 'a' pin
instead (see rst_n_met1's own _comment above for the full pin-swap
evidence). nand_s2.a sits at local (4.98, 2.75) -- INSIDE that same
blob (a single via/pad blob spanning local x 4.455..5.045,
y 0.125..3.74) -- so q now needs exactly the li1 stub escape 'a'
always needed, which used to belong to rst_n's own derivation:
this stage, q_met1 and q_bus below reuse rst_n's pre-#84 nand_s2
geometry byte-for-byte (same re-derived local pin (4.90, 2.71),
not the 'place' stage's own (4.98, 2.75) -- see the historical
derivation note this replaces, preserved in git history at
rst_n_stub's own pre-#84 _comment), since it is the identical
physical conductor and the identical DRC-clean geometry already
proven for it. Only nand_s2's own 'a' pin is escaped here -- q, unlike
the old rst_n bus, touches only NAND_S2, not NAND_M (see the
signal-flow graph in this cell.json's own top _comment: q feeds
NAND_S2 only), so there is no nand_m-side stub to carry forward.
A same-layer (li1/'metal' role, no via) stub carries nand_s2.a
EAST past the blob's east edge (local x=5.045) before any metal2
transition, direction_deg 0 matching sampler_nand2's own 'a' pin
orientation, exactly as rst_n's pre-#84 stub did.

stages.name: q_met1
_comment: q fan-out, step 2 of 4 (issue #84 correction of issue #22's
original recipe): via inv_q's output pin and the stub tip from
q_stub straight up from li1 to met1, zero lateral distance on
each -- the same single-hop via-drop every other fan-out in this
cell uses. inv_q_y's own via here is unchanged from the pre-#84
q_bus stage (it never needed a stub); nand_s2_a_ext's via reuses
rst_n's pre-#84 nand_s2 via geometry byte-for-byte.

stages.name: q_met2
_comment: q fan-out, step 3 of 4 (issue #84 correction of issue #22's
original recipe): the pre-#84 recipe's own long haul stayed on
met1 the whole way, since its destination (nand_s2.en, west of
sampler_nand2's own internal met1 blob) never needed to cross it.
The corrected destination, nand_s2.a, sits on the blob's OWN east
side, and klayout.db against the composed q_met1.gds shows the
blob's own met1 footprint is not a simple rectangle: a 0.17um-wide
bar at local x=43.845..44.015 (global) runs continuously from
y=0.915 up to y=3.53, directly across the straight-line path from
inv_q_y (y=1.2) to nand_s2_a_ext (y=2.71) -- an L-shaped met1 route
at that height band cannot avoid it (confirmed directly: a
same-net-relative overlap of 0.0289um^2 at x=43.845..44.015,
y=1.115..1.285, gen-compose's own diagnostic for 'self-net's
drawn metal overlaps ... block core's own drawn pad metal').
The fix used for rst_n's own pre-#84 'a'-pin bus applies here for
the identical reason: escape to a plane no leaf cell in this
assembly draws on. This stage vias each met1 point straight up to
met2, zero lateral distance -- a single-hop via-drop, the same
mechanic every other met1->met2 transition in this cell uses.
Checked directly against klayout.db (met2 layer, post-q_met1):
the L-shaped path this net's own final stage draws (east at
y=1.2, north at x=44.9) has zero overlap with every other met2
shape already drawn (clk's own basement/vertical network,
clkb_bridge1/clkb_bridge2, mc_bus's own U-lane, and rst_n's own
new bus at y=1.975) even after growing every obstacle by 0.14um
(sky130's own met2.space.1) -- comfortably clear, not a near miss.

stages.name: q_bus
_comment: q fan-out, step 4 of 4 (issue #84 correction of issue #22's
original recipe): design/sampler_core.spice's inv_q's own OUTPUT
(XMiqp/XMiqn's shared drain node) driving NAND_S2's 'a' input
(XMis2na's input-side series NMOS gate, output-adjacent per
sampler_nand2's own leaf pin table) -- inv_q.y (37.9, 1.2) to
nand_s2.a (44.37, 2.75; this stage's own met2 landing sits above
the re-derived (44.9, 2.71) q_met1/q_met2 vias below it).
The cell's own eventual output pin also lands on this net once
top-level promotion happens (not this increment -- see 'What
remains').
Both pins are already on met2 by this stage (via'd in q_met2
above), so this stage's own 'metal3'-role routing draws a plain
met2 wire with no further via -- the same same-layer-continuation
pattern clkb_seg2 already established on met1, applied here one
plane up. The route runs east from (37.9,1.2) to (44.9,1.2), then
north to (44.9,2.71) -- entirely on met2, so nand_s2's own
internal met1 blob (x=43.845..44.435) is on a different layer
and cannot be shorted regardless of the route's own shape; see
q_met2's own _comment for the direct klayout.db clearance check
against every other net already drawn on met2.

stages.name: qb_bus
_comment: qb fan-out (issue #22): the third of the six data-path nets --
design/sampler_core.spice's NAND_S2 OUTPUT node (XMis2pa/XMis2pb's
shared pfet drain and XMis2na's nfet drain) driving TG_FBS's own
'a' terminal (XMfsp/XMfsn's first terminal -- 'XMfsp qb clk s vdd',
so a=qb, ctrl=clk, b=s, per README.md's device-line template).
nand_s2.y (44.18, 0.21) to tg_fbs.a.
One 'metal2'-role (met1) stage, like q -- but for the opposite
reason. q's own nand_s2 pin sat 0.77um WEST of sampler_nand2's
internal met1 blob and could ignore it; qb's own nand_s2 pin is
the blob: measured on the composed sampler_dff.gds (post-q) with
klayout.db, the 0.42um-square met1 landing pad a via-drop puts at
nand_s2.y (x=43.97..44.39, y=0.0..0.42) is entirely CONTAINED in
that blob's own outline, and klt extract already names the blob
net 'mnab_y|mpa_y|mpb_y|nand_s2_y|y' -- it is this very net's own
output via stack, not a foreign obstruction. So unlike q (whose
nand2 'a' pin sits inside the same blob but on a DIFFERENT net --
q, not y -- and therefore needs an li1 stub escape: see q_stub
below, added by issue #84), qb needs no stub at all: the landing
pad merges with metal it is already electrically shorted to.
What the blob does constrain is WHERE the vertical climb runs.
Above y=1.085 the blob narrows to a 0.17um-wide bar at
x=43.845..44.015; a climb centred on the pin's own x=44.18 would
leave an 0.08um same-net notch against that bar's east edge --
under sky130's 0.14um met1.space.1, and a net-unaware deck flags a
same-net notch. The climb is therefore jogged 0.17um east first,
to x=44.35 (wire x=44.265..44.435): that column is an exact
overlay on the blob's own y=0.42..0.915 section (x=44.265..44.435)
and clears the narrow bar by 0.25um everywhere above it. The
y=0.21 jog itself (x=44.18..44.35, wire y=0.125..0.295) is fully
inside the blob's own x=43.97..44.435 bottom section.
The long haul then runs east on met1 at y=2.0 -- the only free
met1 lane between clkb_bus's own east segment (top edge y=1.24,
0.675um below) and clk_bus's own via-drop pad at tg_fbs_ctrl
stage was derived, rst_n's own met1 via pad at nand_s2_a
(x=44.69..45.11, y=2.5..2.92) cleared by 0.415um and q's own met1
(east edge x=43.285) by 0.56um; issue #84 later moved q onto
nand_s2_a (see q_stub/q_met1/q_bus below) -- re-verified DRC-clean
against this stage's own unchanged geometry as part of that fix,
not re-derived here. Nothing else is drawn on met1 east of
x=44.435 below the vdd bus.
The destination port is declared at (50.2, 0.21), NOT at the
(50.385, 1.2) the README's own sampler_tg port table uses. Same
physical conductor -- klayout.db shows tg_fbs's 'a' li1 strap is a
single polygon, SOLID from x=49.155 to x=50.47 across
y=0.125..0.295, while at y=1.2 it is only the 0.17um-wide vertical
at x=50.3..50.47 -- but a 0.42um landing pad centred on (50.385,
1.2) spans x=50.175..50.595 and would push the cell's own east
bbox edge from 50.47 out to 50.595, hanging met1 off the
easternmost instance's face. tg_fbs is the last block in the row,
so that overhang is the one place in this cell where a landing pad
grows the cell rather than filling it.
x=50.2 (not the round 50.0 tried first) because the landing pad is
drawn on li1 as well as met1, and li1 is where the strap's own
shape bites. At (50.0, 0.21) the li1 pad spans x=49.79..50.21, and
its east edge lands 0.09um short of the strap's own vertical
section (west edge x=50.3, present for y>0.295) -- under sky130's
0.17um li1.space.1, and gen-compose refused the leg for exactly
that reason ('draws a pad ... within 0.09um of block core's own
drawn geometry'). Shifting 0.2um east makes the pad OVERLAP that
vertical instead of nearly missing it (pad x=49.99..50.41 vs the
vertical's 50.3..50.47, same net, so they merge into one shape),
while its west edge stays 0.415um clear of the strap's own
x=49.155..49.575 lower stub and its east edge stays 0.06um inside
the cell's own east bbox edge. Re-checked directly on klayout.db:
a 0.17um li1 space_check over the whole strap plus the pad reports
0 violations at x=50.2 (and the 1 gen-compose reported at 50.0).
On met1 the same pad spans x=49.99..50.41 -- 0.75um clear of
clkb_bus's own met1 (east edge 49.24) and 0.29um clear of the vss
bus (top edge -0.29).
Still open (issue #22 / #27): m, mb, s, and promoting the
whole-cell external pins (d/clk/rst_n/q/vdd/vss) once all six
data-path nets exist -- see layout/sampler_dff/README.md's 'What
remains' section.

stages.name: s_met1
_comment: s fan-out, stage 1 of 2 (issue #22): the fourth of the six
data-path nets, and the first three-pin one. s is the slave
latch's own storage node -- TG_S's pass output, inv_q's input and
TG_FBS's feedback return: 'XMtsp mb clkb s vdd' / 'XMfsp qb clk s
vdd' put s on BOTH transmission gates' third terminal, i.e. their
'b' pin per README.md's device-line template, and inv_q's own
gate pair (XMiqp/XMiqn) is its third leg. tg_s.b (28.895, 1.2),
This stage does nothing but via all three li1 pins straight up to
met1, zero lateral distance -- the same single-hop via-drop
clk_met1 and mc_met1 already use, three times. It exists because
the long haul below runs on met2 ('metal3' role), which is two via
hops from li1 and gen-compose's via-drop is single-hop only.
s fan-out, stage 2 of 2 (issue #22): the met2 long haul, 23.64um
end to end across two thirds of the cell, steered leg-by-leg with
connectivity[].legs[] (klayout-tools #1529 -- waypoints_um is
rejected outright on a >2-pin net, the same reason clk_bus needed
legs[]).
met1 cannot carry this net. Measured on the composed
sampler_dff.gds (post-qb) with klayout.db, every met1 lane between
the pins' own y=1.2 and the vdd bus (y>=4.03) is blocked at at
least two columns across this span: q's own L-lane occupies
x=37.69..43.285 at y=0.99..2.185 (squarely between inv_q and
nand_s2), qb's own east run occupies x=44.265..50.285 at y up to
2.085, clkb_bus's east segment occupies x=44.69..49.115 at
y=0.19..0.61, sampler_nand2's own internal met1 blob runs
x=43.845..44.015 from y=0.19 all the way to y=3.53, and
clkb_seg2's own x=30.34 vertical (drawn x=30.2..30.5,
y=0.315..2.415) stands in the way at the west end. met2 over the
same span is all but empty: the only 69/20 drawn between x=28.6
and x=48.4 in the band y=0.9..2.4 is clk_bus's own via-drop pad at
tg_s_ctrlb (x=29.53..29.95, y=0.82..1.24), and east of x=30 that
band is completely empty out to clk_bus's own tg_fbs_ctrl vertical
(x=48.945..49.115, 0.55um east of this net's own east landing
pad). rst_n_bus's own met2 backbone (y=2.5..2.92) is the nearest
neighbour above, 0.715um clear of this lane.
CORRECTION (issue #84): the two paragraphs above describe the
pre-#84 cell and are kept for the met1 finding, which still holds
-- but two of the met1 obstacles they name have MOVED and the met2
band they call 'all but empty' no longer is. q's met1 L-lane is
gone (q's long haul is on met2 now, since its corrected
destination nand_s2.a sits east of sampler_nand2's own met1 blob),
and in its place met2 now carries q's east climb
(x=44.69..45.11, y=2.5..2.92), while rst_n's corrected via pad at
nand_s2.en occupies x=42.865..43.285 from y=1.765 up and its
backbone dropped from y=2.5..2.92 to y=2.115..2.285. s's span
(36.545..48.185) strictly contains q's (37.9..44.9) with q below
this lane at one end and above it at the other, so the two MUST
cross and sky130's curated deck exposes no fourth plane to cross
on (_PDK_ROLE_LAYERS tops out at 'metal3'/met2). gen-compose
confirms it directly: the unchanged straight lane comes back as
'nets left unrouted by gen-compose: [s]'. Leg 2 is therefore
re-steered around q -- y=1.7 east to x=40.0, a 0.175um dip to
y=1.525 (the exact middle of the 0.48um window between q's own
east lane at y<=1.285 and rst_n's en pad at y>=1.765) out to
x=44.0, a climb at the one column clear of both rst_n's backbone
(east edge 43.285) and q's climb (west edge 44.815), then east at
y=3.2 -- the first lane clear of q's landing pad, above which met2
is empty across x=20..55 -- and back down at x=48.185. Tightest
new-to-existing met2 gap 0.1555um against sky130's own 0.14um
met2.space.1; DRC clean, 0 violations, bbox unchanged, net_count
still 18. leg 1, the s_met1 stage and all three via-drop pads are
unchanged. See layout/sampler_dff/README.md's 'Re-derivation of
the s long haul (issue #84)'.
The lane still meets inv_q.a at y=1.7 -- the MIDDLE pin's own y --
and, before #84, ran straight across at that height with a 0.5um
jog up at the west pin and down at the east one, so it passes
straight through inv_q.a's own via-drop pad instead of stopping
short of it. The round y=2.0 was tried first and was NOT
DRC-clean: exactly one met2.space.1 violation, an 0.005um same-net
notch at x=36.63..36.895, y=1.910..1.915, between that pad's own
top edge (the pad is 0.42um square about y=1.7, so it reaches
1.91) and a 0.17um-wide lane centred on y=2.0 (which starts at
1.915). The two shapes are the same net and are joined through the
drop wire between them, but they are DRAWN 5nm apart and a
net-unaware deck flags that exactly as it would a foreign gap --
the same class of same-net notch qb's own jogged climb avoids, at
5nm instead of 80nm. Running the lane at the pin's own y makes the
pad and the lane overlap instead of nearly touching, and drops a
corner from the route.
Clearances measured on the composed GDS (minimum edge-to-edge,
this increment's own geometry to the nearest foreign shape):
met1 0.425um to clk_bus's own met1 pads at both columns, 0.505um
to clkb_bus's east segment below tg_fbs.b and 0.505um to qb's own
east met1 run above it; li1 0.425um to clk_bus's own li1 pads and
1.06um to inv_q's own internal li1 at x=37.815 (all three
unchanged by #84 -- this stage adds no met1 or li1 geometry). At
inv_q.a the pad lands between that pin's own two existing li1 gate
leaving 0.25um and 0.38um same-net gaps -- both over sky130's
0.17um li1.space.1. On met2 the pre-#84 figures (0.375um to
clk_bus's tg_s_ctrlb pad, 0.55um to its tg_fbs_ctrl vertical,
0.715um to rst_n_bus's backbone) are superseded by the re-steered
route's own measurement: 0.1555um minimum, in the dip under
rst_n's en pad. The tightest same-net gap the lane itself leaves
is 0.205um, between the west landing pad's top edge (y=1.41) and
the lane's own bottom edge (y=1.615).
Still open (issue #22 / #27): m and mb. The sampler_nand2 input
swap (#84) is fixed as of this cell.json, and the whole-cell
external pins (d/clk/rst_n/q/vdd/vss) are all promoted -- see
layout/sampler_dff/README.md's 'What remains' section.
